summary: Five parallel work packages with disjoint files. WP1 (player shell) lands the per-round seed: a new `seedScope` on GameModule (default 'round' → seed = round.id; Trivia sets 'player' → `${round.id}:${playerRowId}`, ADR-027), plus the two shell-flow fixes (a round ended during the phone's 3-2-1 submits nothing; a 5 s round-row safety refetch while a game is on screen). WP2 (How Many? phone) makes the whole step chain a fixed schedule anchored on stored epochs (intro on roundStartEpoch, lock on the answer's end, next look on the lock's end, runDue catches up in a loop), which fixes the reload/lock/hidden-page timing findings and keeps the 40 s worst case; the hidden-look flash skip stays as documented. WP3 (host) anchors the H3 reveal on ended_at (dots and crowd average computed from the round's end, late rows at once), compresses the How Many? schedule (dots 3.5 s, mean 4.0 s), documents the ≥ 3-row mode caveat and adds the missing Intermission/timing tests. WP4 (Pairs + Swipe Sort phones) measures Pairs' clear_ms on the epoch clock, adds Pairs' visibilitychange handler, flips unmatched cards down on timeout, anchors both board clocks on roundStartEpoch + 1500, lets a press during a Swipe Sort gap sort the next item, fixes the stale-drag offset, the idle 36→37 example (doc, unit test, pgTAP 11) and the outline-offset token. WP5 (shared docs) writes ADR-137 recording these behaviour changes, OQ-23 for the 128 s hold (ADR-017 is locked), and syncs SCORING/SCREENS/SESSION_LIFECYCLE/ARCHITECTURE/TESTING/games-v3. Not fixed: host-side-2 (needs a team decision on ADR-017).

work_packages.title: Per-round game seed (Trivia stays per player) + shell flow fixes
work_packages.instructions:
ROOT CAUSE A (seed): src/player/PlayerApp.tsx:250 persists `seed: `${round.id}:${playerRowId}`` and :355 falls back to the same, so every phone draws its own How Many? fields, Pairs board, Swipe Sort / Color Clash / Close the Brackets sequences and Odd One Out layout, while the docs, ADR-134 (2), ADR-136 (1) and src/host/howManyStrips.ts (mode of true_count) all assume one seed per round. Trivia (ADR-027: per-player draw + per-player option shuffle) is the only game that wants a per-player seed.

CHANGE A:
1. src/games/types.ts: add to `GameModule` an optional `seedScope?: 'round' | 'player'` with a doc comment: `'round'` (default) = every phone in the round gets the same seed (`round.id`), required by games whose content is shared and by the H3 How Many? reveal; `'player'` = `${round.id}:${playerRowId}` for games whose doc asks for per-player variety (Trivia, ADR-027). Update the `GameProps.seed` comment to say 'Per-round seed (reload-stable; per player only for seedScope: player)'.
2. src/games/trivia/index.ts: add `seedScope: 'player'` to the `trivia` module.
3. New src/player/seed.ts: `export function gameSeed(game: GameId, roundId: string, playerRowId: string): string` that reads `games[game]?.seedScope` from `src/games/registry` and returns `roundId` for 'round'/undefined/unregistered game, `${roundId}:${playerRowId}` for 'player'. Pure, no React.
4. src/player/PlayerApp.tsx: line 250 → `seed: gameSeed(round.game, round.id, playerRowId)`; line 355 fallback → `String(local.seed ?? gameSeed(view.round.id ? view.round.game : ..., view.round.id, playerRowId))` (same helper). Keep persisting the seed actually used in `local.seed` (e2e/helpers.ts `readSeed` reads `gdg.v1.current.seed`; do not touch e2e). Existing phones with an old persisted per-player seed mid-round keep it (harmless; the snapshot rule wins).
5. docs/games/trivia.md: in §2 heading/first line say the draw uses the per-PLAYER seed (`<round id>:<player row id>`, `seedScope: 'player'`, ADR-027) and that every other game uses the round id; keep the rest.

ROOT CAUSE B (round ended during the 3-2-1): src/player/playerFlow.ts:104-110: `isRoundEndedLocally` is true when `round.status === 'done'` regardless of `now < roundStartEpoch`, so the game mounts with `roundEnded: true`, every module calls finishNow at mount and a 0-score row is inserted for a player who never saw the game (violates SESSION_LIFECYCLE §5 'submits nothing' and ADR-014).
CHANGE B: in `derivePlayerView`, inside the localRound block compute `ended`; if `ended && now < local.roundStartEpoch` (only possible via server 'done'; the 120 s cap can't pass before the start) treat the round as never played: skip the block (fall through to the results/playing/intermission logic; do NOT return 'game'). Add a comment referencing E26/E27 and ADR-014. Optionally in PlayerApp add a tiny effect: when `view.screen` is neither 'intro' nor 'game' and `local.roundId` is set for a round that is done and `local.roundStartEpoch > Date.now()`, `update(() => ({ roundId: null, roundStartEpoch: null, gameSnapshot: null }))` so `inRound` stops the 250 ms clock; keep it minimal.

ROOT CAUSE C (missed round-end event): src/player/hooks.ts:22 `STATE_SAFETY_REFETCH_MS = 15_000` equals `LATE_ACCEPT_MS` (config.ts), so a phone that misses the rounds UPDATE (socket still SUBSCRIBED, tab visible) can learn of the end up to 15 s later and submit after GD007.
CHANGE C: add `const ROUND_SAFETY_REFETCH_MS = 5000` and a third parameter `useSessionSync(sessionId, playerRowId, inRound = false)`; while `inRound` is true run an extra `window.setInterval` every 5 s that calls only `fetchRounds(sessionId)` and `setRounds(prev => replaceEqualDeep(prev, r))` (one small request, not the triple `load()`); clear it when `inRound` flips false. PlayerApp passes the existing `inRound` boolean (line 228; it is computed after `sync` today, so pass a derived value from `local` computed before the hook: `local.roundId !== null && !local.submittedRounds.includes(local.roundId)`). Keep the 15 s full refetch. Do not add realtime subscriptions (ADR-112).

EDGE CASES: gameSeed for a game absent from the registry (Trivia with < 5 questions) returns the round id. `local.seed` may be a number in old storage (type `string | number | null`): keep `String(...)`. Tests must not import React for seed.ts.
work_packages.tests_to_add: src/player/seed.test.ts: (1) `gameSeed('how_many', R, A) === gameSeed('how_many', R, B) === R` and the same for 'pairs', 'swipe_sort', 'close_brackets', 'color_clash', 'odd_one_out', 'simon', 'stop_the_clock', 'perfect_circle'; (2) `gameSeed('trivia', R, A) !== gameSeed('trivia', R, B)` and both start with `R:`; (3) `fieldFor(gameSeed('how_many', R, A), i).count === fieldFor(gameSeed('how_many', R, B), i).count` for i = 0..2 and `layoutFor(...)` equal for Pairs (import from the game packages, read-only). src/player/playerFlow.test.ts: 'a round that ended while the phone was still in its 3-2-1 is not mounted' → round.status 'done', roundStartEpoch = T0+3000, now = T0+1000 → screen is not 'game' and not 'intro' (round_result/intermission per the rest of the state), and viewKey differs from the game key. src/player/hooks.test.tsx (new, vi.mock('../lib/api') + vi.mock('../lib/realtime')): with fake timers, `useSessionSync(s, p, true)` calls `fetchRounds` again within 5 s; with `false` it does not before 15 s.

work_packages.title: How Many? phone: fixed step schedule anchored on epochs (intro, lock, look, hidden page)
work_packages.instructions:
ROOT CAUSE: src/games/how-many/HowMany.tsx anchors only the answer deadline on stored epochs. The intro timer (line 312-316) runs HM_INTRO_MS from mount; `lock()` (line 272) sets `lockedEndEpoch = Date.now() + 500`; `startLook()` (line 244) sets `lookStartEpoch = Date.now()`; the `locked` branch of runDue (347-349) starts the next look whenever the late timer fires. So every reload, screen lock, JS freeze or hidden tab pushes the remaining flashes later (measured 57-70 s rounds against `worstCaseMs` 40 000; ADR-018 'a reload never resets a clock'; E15 'any attempt whose timeout passed is closed with its timeout rule'), and while hidden with timers still firing the game runs every flash by itself with no bound. Also (uncertain finding) `dueEpoch` returns null for phase 'flash' while `flashStartEpoch` is still null (the post-paint effect at 319-322), the only state with no deadline.

DECISION (recorded by WP5 as ADR-137 (2); implement exactly this): How Many? is a FIXED SCHEDULE anchored on `roundStartEpoch` and on the player's own OK taps. Every step boundary is derived from stored epochs, never from the time a timer happened to fire:
- look_0 starts at `roundStartEpoch + HM_INTRO_MS`.
- flash window = `lookStartEpoch + 1000 … + 2000`; answerStartEpoch = end of the flash window (unchanged).
- answer ends at the OK tap epoch (Date.now() at the tap, only when visible and live) or at `answerStartEpoch + HM_ANSWER_MS` on timeout; `lockedEndEpoch = answerEnd + HM_LOCKED_MS` (NOT Date.now() + 500).
- look_{i+1} starts at `lockedEndEpoch_i` (NOT Date.now()).
- A look whose window is already over when it is processed (late timer > 250 ms, hidden page, reload) skips the flash exactly as today (documented §3/§9); its answer runs from `lookStartEpoch + 2000`; if that has also passed, the answer times out with `guess: parseGuess(typed)` (null on a fresh look) and the chain continues, so a phone that comes back after a long lock closes everything overdue at once and finishes ≤ roundStartEpoch + 39 s + processing.
- The hidden-look flash skip is unchanged; a hidden page never pauses the schedule (that is the bounded version of G2-3's 'plays itself': the answers time out on schedule and the round always ends inside the worst case).

CHANGES in HowMany.tsx:
1. `startLook(roundIndex, at: number)` sets `lookStartEpoch: at`. Intro: `dueEpoch` returns `roundStartEpoch + HM_INTRO_MS` for phase 'intro' (pass roundStartEpoch into dueEpoch, or read the ref inside runDue); delete the separate intro effect (the single scheduler handles it) or arm it for `Math.max(0, roundStartEpoch + HM_INTRO_MS - Date.now())`; runDue's 'intro' branch calls `startLook(0, roundStartEpoch + HM_INTRO_MS)`.
2. `lock(round, answerEnd: number)` sets `lockedEndEpoch: answerEnd + HM_LOCKED_MS`; handleKey OK passes `now`; the answer-timeout branch passes `current.answerStartEpoch + HM_ANSWER_MS`.
3. runDue 'locked' branch: `startLook(current.rounds.length, current.lockedEndEpoch)`.
4. Make runDue a catch-up loop: apply one due step, then re-read `stateRef.current` and repeat while `dueEpoch` ≤ now (guard with a max of ~12 iterations); return true if anything was applied. The flash branch (`now <= due + HM_FLASH_LATE_MS && !isHidden()`) is kept as is; after the bare `setState` for 'flash' stop the loop (the flash needs a paint).
5. `dueEpoch`: phase 'flash' with `flashStartEpoch === null` → `lookStartEpoch + HM_LOOK_MS + HM_FLASH_MS` (latest allowed end), so a freeze between the setState and the post-paint effect still has a deadline; when that fires with a null epoch, startAnswer(lookStart + 2000, null).
6. Keep the visibilitychange handler; also listen to `pageshow` (bfcache) calling the same runDue. Keep `resumeSnapshot` (reload rules) but note the 'locked' and 'intro' resumes are now covered by the loop (a snapshot with a past `lockedEndEpoch` starts look_{i+1} at that epoch, and if its window is over goes straight to the answer/timeout chain).
7. Update the file header comment and the `HM_FLASH_LATE_MS` comment to describe the fixed schedule.

EDGE CASES: the OK tap must still be refused after `answerStartEpoch + HM_ANSWER_MS` (unchanged). An OK tap epoch is always ≤ the timeout epoch, so `lockedEndEpoch` never exceeds the schedule. `finishNow` on `roundEnded` unchanged. Reduced motion unchanged. Idle worst case: 1.5 + 3 × 12.5 = 39 s exactly, `worstCaseMs` 40 000 unchanged; `src/games/worstCase.test.tsx` must stay green (adjust only if its fake-timer sequencing assumed the mount-anchored intro).

DOCS (docs/games/how-many.md): §3 'Flow and timings': state the fixed schedule (the bullets above) and that the game clock is `roundStartEpoch`-anchored; §9 add rows 'Reload during the intro' (look_0 still at roundStartEpoch + 1.5 s; if that passed, the look/flash rules apply from that epoch), 'Reload during `locked` after lockedEndEpoch' (the next look counts from lockedEndEpoch; a passed window skips the flash), 'Long screen lock / JS freeze' (every step whose epoch passed is closed with its rule on return; the round ends by its worst case + the resume; flashes missed while locked are timed out, never replayed), 'Page hidden but timers running (background tab, covered window)' (same schedule; flashes that end hidden are skipped; a returning player is on whatever step the schedule says); update 'Screen lock during the look/flash' rows to reference the schedule; §10 add HM-T15..T18 for the new tests. Reference ADR-137 (2).
work_packages.tests_to_add: HowMany.test.tsx (fake timers, real component): (1) reload during the intro: mount at roundStart+3400 with snapshot null → first `lookStartEpoch === roundStart + 1500`, the flash is skipped (window passed) and the pad shows with the deadline `roundStart + 1500 + 2000 + 10000`; (2) answer 1 open at 4 s, `vi.setSystemTime(+40 s)` without advancing timers, dispatch visibilitychange → onFinish at once, rounds 2-3 `timed_out: true, guess: null`, `durationMs ≤ 40 000 + 100`; (3) reload in 'locked' with `lockedEndEpoch` 3 s in the past → next `lookStartEpoch === lockedEndEpoch` (not mount time) and phase 'answer' with `answerStartEpoch === lockedEndEpoch + 2000`; (4) OK tap at answerStart+2 s → `lockedEndEpoch === tapEpoch + 500` and the next look starts there; (5) document.visibilityState mocked 'hidden' from the intro with timers firing → each look ends without a field (`hm-field` never rendered), each answer times out at its schedule, finish at roundStart + 39 000 ± one tick; (6) phase 'flash' with `flashStartEpoch` null has a due of `lookStart + 2000` (unit-test `dueEpoch` by exporting it, or via a snapshot render). Keep every existing HM-T test green.

work_packages.title: Host H3 How Many? reveal anchored on ended_at, compressed schedule, tie caveat, missing tests
work_packages.instructions:
ROOT CAUSE: the 7 s round-board step is anchored on the round's `ended_at` (schedule.ts, useHost.ts, ADR-129 (1)), but the reveal's dot bursts (`RevealIn` → `ShatterBurst delay` = 'ms after mount') and the crowd-average marker (`HM_REVEAL_MEAN_MS` 5200 from mount, HowManyReveal.tsx:62/77) count from the moment HowManyReveal mounts with rows, which is ~0.6 s (local) to > 1.5 s (hotspot/reload) after ended_at. Measured: the mean is visible for 1.3-1.4 s, never after a host reload. Late rows (E22, refetch on scoresVersion) mount their dots and a first-time mean with fresh delays that can land after the step ends.

CHANGES:
1. src/host/reveal.ts: extend `RevealProps` with optional `anchorMs?: number` = the LOCAL-clock epoch of the round's `ended_at` (server time minus the host offset). Add a pure helper `export function slotDelay(anchorMs: number | null, delayMs: number, nowMs = Date.now()): number` returning `delayMs` when anchor is null (preview/fixtures: unchanged behaviour) else `Math.max(0, anchorMs + delayMs - nowMs)`. Unit-test it in howManyStrips.test.ts or HowManyReveal.test.tsx.
2. src/host/Intermission.tsx: compute `const anchorMs = round.ended_at ? Date.parse(round.ended_at) - (host.offset ?? 0) : null` and pass `anchorMs={anchorMs}` to both `<Reveal …>` renders (live and preview). Nothing else changes; the step boundaries stay in schedule.ts.
3. src/host/StcReveal.tsx `RevealTrack`: accept `anchorMs?: number | null` and pass `delayMs={slotDelay(anchorMs ?? null, slots[j]?.delayMs ?? 0)}` to each dot's RevealIn; when the computed delay is 0 and anchor is not null (already due, e.g. a late row or a reload mid-step) pass `shards={0}` so it appears at once without a burst. StcReveal passes its `anchorMs` through (Stop the Clock benefits from the same anchoring; no timing constants change for it).
4. src/host/HowManyReveal.tsx: pass `anchorMs` to RevealTrack; the mean line and marker use `delayMs={slotDelay(anchorMs ?? null, HM_REVEAL_MEAN_MS)}` and `shards={0}`. Build the plan with the compressed schedule: `revealSchedule(counts, { totalMs: HM_REVEAL_DOTS_MS })` (plays.ts already accepts `totalMs`). Update the header comment (dots within 3.5 s, mean at 4.0 s, everything measured from ended_at, late rows at once).
5. src/config.ts: `HM_REVEAL_MEAN_MS = 4000` (comment: 'fades in this long after `rounds.ended_at`, leaving ≥ 3 s of the 7 s step for the whole picture') and new `HM_REVEAL_DOTS_MS = 3500` ('the How Many? dots burst in within this long after ended_at'). Do not change the 7 s step (ADR-117/129).
6. src/host/howManyStrips.ts: the `modeOf` comment: state that the 'one tampered row can't move the axis' rule needs ≥ 3 rows; with 1-2 rows (a tie) the higher-ranked row's value wins; keep the behaviour (cheating is an accepted risk, ADR-021). Also note that since ADR-137 (1) every row carries the same true_count, so the mode is normally unanimous.
7. Tests (host-side-5): Intermission.test.tsx gains a `how_many` round case (layout 'reveal', `hm-reveal` rendered via preview rows, `data-step` round_board) and the last-round (isLast) variant; HowManyReveal.test.tsx gains timing tests against the anchor (below). Keep all existing host tests green (94).

EDGE CASES: `host.offset` null → anchor uses offset 0. Dev fixtures (src/dev/fixtures/host.tsx, not in this package) pass no anchor → old mount-relative timing, must still compile. A remount after a host reload 6 s into the step shows all dots and the mean immediately (delay 0, no shards). Reduced motion path unchanged (200 ms fades).
work_packages.tests_to_add: HowManyReveal.test.tsx: (1) with `anchorMs = Date.now() - 1500` at mount, the mean (`hm-mean`) is visible at mount + (4000 − 1500) and all dots by mount + (3500 − 1500) + burst; (2) with `anchorMs = Date.now() - 6000` (reload late in the step) every dot and the mean are visible on the first frame after rows arrive; (3) rerender with an extra row 2.7 s into the step → its dots appear at `max(0, slot − elapsed)` i.e. at once when overdue, and a flash whose first guess arrives late shows its mean at `max(0, 4000 − elapsed)`; (4) `slotDelay` unit cases (null anchor passthrough, clamp at 0). howManyStrips.test.ts: (5) rows with mixed true_counts → count is the mode; (6) 2-row tie → the first (higher-ranked) row's value, documenting the ≥ 3-row caveat; (7) a 5-row set where 4 agree and 1 differs → the agreed value. Intermission.test.tsx: how_many reveal layout and last-round variant.

work_packages.title: Pairs and Swipe Sort phones: epoch clear time, visibility handler, anchored board clocks, gap press, stale drag, idle 37, token
work_packages.instructions:
PAIRS (src/games/pairs/Pairs.tsx):
A. clear_ms on the epoch clock (G4-1/G2-2/pairs-timing-02). Root cause: line 189 measures the 8th match with `performance.now() − perfStartRef` (set once at line 209), a monotonic clock that stops during a real OS sleep on iOS/Android, while the 60 s end (167, 219-225) and the countdown (270-272) use Date.now(); a sleep mid-game shrinks clear_ms (score up to 1000, countdown jumps from ~24 back to ~54 at the clear) or pushes it under `pr.too_fast`. Change: `const clearMs = Math.max(0, Math.min(now - gameStart, PR_GAME_MS))` at the 8th match; delete `perfStartRef` entirely (the ms precision of Date.now() is enough for a 6 points/s slope). Keep `nowPerf` only if still needed elsewhere (it is not). Update the header comment. docs/games/pairs.md §4 'Measurement' line 48: `clear_ms` is `Date.now()` at the `pointerdown` of the eighth match minus `gameStartEpoch` (the same epoch clock as the 60 s end, so a sleep never shortens it), rounded and capped at 60 000; §9 'Screen lock' row: add 'and the clear time includes the lock'.
B. Visibility handler (G2-1). Root cause: Pairs has no visibilitychange/pageshow listener (HowMany.tsx:368-374 and SwipeSort.tsx:257-259 do), so after a device sleep past the 60 s end the stalled timer leaves the board at 0 with taps ignored for up to ~55 s. Change: extract the scheduler body into `runDue()` (reads stateRef: game end → finishNow(); passed lock → commit faceUp [] / lockUntilEpoch null; else nothing) and call it from the timer, from a `visibilitychange` (when visible) and `pageshow` listener, and bump `wake`/`tick` on return so the countdown re-renders and the timer re-arms.
C. Timeout with cards up (pairs-timing-03): in `finishNow`, when `clearEpoch === null` commit `faceUp: []` (unfound cards go down, pairs.md §6 'done' and §9 'not revealed'); the score is unaffected.
D. Board clock anchored on roundStartEpoch (shell-resume-roundend-3): the intro effect arms `Math.max(0, roundStartEpoch + INTRO_MS - Date.now())` and commits `gameStartEpoch: roundStartEpoch + INTRO_MS` (fixed, never Date.now()), so a hidden/late phone's 60 s board still ends at roundStartEpoch + 61.5 s (worst case 62 s, E15 clocks never pause). If the mount is already past that epoch the board appears at once with the remaining time (and finishes at once if ≥ 60 s passed). pairs.md §3 + §9 ('Reload/hidden during the intro' row: the board clock started at roundStartEpoch + 1.5 s regardless).

SWIPE SORT (src/games/swipe-sort/SwipeSort.tsx):
E. Anchored intro like D: `gameStartEpoch = itemStartEpoch = roundStartEpoch + INTRO_MS`, timer armed on the remaining time; if the mount is later than that, `runTimeline`'s catchUp counts the missed items (existing logic). `perfStartRef` = `performance.now() − (Date.now() − itemStartEpoch)` as the reload effect (line 296-302) already does. docs/games/swipe-sort.md §3 note + §9 row.
F. Press during a gap sorts the next item (swipe-timing-gap-press-dead; behaviour change recorded by WP5 as ADR-137 (4)). Root cause: handlePointerDown returns before tracking when `gapEndEpoch !== null`, and handlePointerMove drops the rest of that touch. Change: in handlePointerDown, when phase is 'play' and `gapEndEpoch !== null` (a gap), still run reduceGesture/setPointerCapture and set `dragItemRef.current = current.itemIndex + 1`; keep ignoring presses during the intro and after the game end. Keep a `lastPointRef {x,y}` updated on every pointermove of the tracked pointer. In `runTimeline`, when the committed `next.itemStartEpoch !== current.itemStartEpoch` and `gestureRef.current.pointerId !== null && dragItemRef.current === next.itemIndex`, re-base `gestureRef.current = { ...gestureRef.current, startX: lastPoint.x, startY: lastPoint.y }` so the 40 px and `swipe_ms` count from the item's onset (ss.too_fast still holds). Docs §3 line 57 → 'Presses during the intro are ignored; a press that starts during a gap arms the NEXT item: the 40 px count from where the finger is when the chevron appears'; §9 'Press during a gap' row updated the same way; §10 add SS-T15.
G. Stale drag (swipe-timing-stale-drag-follows-next-item): in handlePointerMove call `setDrag(step.dx)` only when `dragItemRef.current === stateRef.current.itemIndex && stateRef.current.itemStartEpoch !== null`, else `setDrag(0)`; in `registerSwipe` call `setDrag(0)` on every early return that happens after the gesture was consumed (item mismatch, gap, past deadline/game end). With F, a pre-armed gap press must not move the flying-off chevron (dragItemRef ≠ itemIndex until the next item is live).
H. Idle example 36 → 37 (swipe-timing-idle-example-36/G1-5): docs/games/swipe-sort.md §4 table row E → `0 / 0 / 37`; src/games/swipe-sort/scoring.test.ts lines 12 and 36 → 37; supabase/tests/11_score_bounds_swipe_sort.sql line ~72 fixture and line ~105 label → 37 (no migration: the bound is missed ≤ 80; the plan count stays the same). SCORING.md §3.9 is WP5's.
I. Token (player-ui-i18n-001): SwipeSort.module.css `.zoneCorrect { outline-offset: var(--focus-offset); }` (same 2 px). Leave the shake keyframes (repo-wide convention).

EDGE CASES: Pairs taps at/after `gameStart + 60 000` stay ignored; a tap that beats the late lock timer still resolves the lock first (unchanged). Swipe Sort: `finishNow` resets gestureRef; a pre-armed press when the game ends is dropped with setDrag(0). Reduced motion: setDrag is a no-op (unchanged).
work_packages.tests_to_add: Pairs.test.tsx: (1) fake timers with `toFake` including 'performance' and 'Date': match 1 pair, `vi.setSystemTime(+30 s)` without advancing timers, clear the rest → `clear_ms` equals the Date.now() elapsed (≥ 30 000), score < 1000, `pr-seconds` never increases at the clear; (2) live suspend: board+20 s, `vi.setSystemTime(+50 s)`, dispatch visibilitychange → onFinish at once with `times_up`; (3) suspend across a lock end → cards flip back on visibilitychange; (4) mismatch tapped at 59.9 s then timeout → both tiles `data-state 'down'`; (5) mount 30 s after roundStartEpoch (hidden intro) → board shows with 30 s left and `gameStartEpoch === roundStartEpoch + 1500`; durationMs ≤ 62 000 in the idle case. SwipeSort.test.tsx: (6) reload/mount 5 s late → `gameStartEpoch === roundStartEpoch + 1500` and missed items counted; (7) SS-T15: correct swipe on item 0, pointerdown during the gap, advance 200 ms, move 60 then 120 px the correct way → correct 2, swipe_ms counted from the onset; (8) stale drag: drag started on item 0 held through its miss, move +30 px on item 1 → `--ss-drag` stays '0px' on item 1's chevron and a +80 px move counts nothing; (9) registerSwipe past the deadline resets `--ss-drag` to 0. scoring.test.ts: idle example with 37. pgTAP 11: fixture 37, label updated.

work_packages.title: Shared docs: ADR-137, OQ-23 (128 s hold), SCORING/SCREENS/SESSION_LIFECYCLE/ARCHITECTURE/TESTING/games-v3 sync
work_packages.instructions:
Write these exactly (the code packages run in parallel and implement precisely what is described here; do not wait for them).

1. docs/DECISIONS.md: append `### ADR-137 Phase 8 timing and seeding fixes` — **Proposed** · investigation `docs/investigations/2026-09-25-phase8-games/` (2026-09-25). Context: the seed was per player (`${round.id}:${playerRowId}`, PlayerApp.tsx), against ADR-134 (2)/ADR-136 (1); How Many?, Pairs and Swipe Sort chained their steps on the time late timers fired; Pairs measured `clear_ms` on `performance.now()`, which stops during a device sleep; the H3 reveal counted from its mount, not `ended_at`. Decision: (1) **Seed scope**: `GameModule.seedScope` = `'round'` (default; seed = `round.id`, every phone in a round sees the same fields/boards/sequences) or `'player'` (`${round.id}:${playerRowId}`; only Trivia, ADR-027). (2) **How Many? fixed schedule**: look 1 at `roundStartEpoch + 1.5 s`; flash window `look + 1 … + 2 s`; answer ends at the OK tap or `+ 10 s`; locked = answer end `+ 0.5 s`; the next look starts at the lock's end. Timers never move an anchor: after a reload, screen lock, freeze or hidden tab every step whose epoch passed is closed with its rule on return (a passed look skips the flash as before, ADR-136; a passed answer is a timeout); a hidden page never pauses the schedule, so a phone away for 30 s loses those flashes and the round still ends inside its 39 s worst case (E15, ADR-018). (3) **Pairs / Swipe Sort board clocks** start at `roundStartEpoch + 1.5 s` whatever the mount time; Pairs' `clear_ms` = `Date.now()` at the eighth match minus `gameStartEpoch` (same clock as the 60 s end); Pairs closes passed locks/ends on `visibilitychange`/`pageshow` like the other games; a timed-out board shows unfound cards face down. (4) **Swipe Sort gap press**: a press that starts during the 0.15 s gap arms the next item (the 40 px and `swipe_ms` count from that item's onset); intro presses stay ignored; a drag can only move the item it is armed for. (5) **H3 reveal anchoring**: dot and crowd-average delays are measured from `rounds.ended_at` (host offset), late rows and a reloaded host show what is due at once; How Many? dots within 3.5 s and the mean at 4.0 s (`HM_REVEAL_DOTS_MS`, `HM_REVEAL_MEAN_MS`), the 7 s step unchanged (ADR-117/129). (6) The 'one tampered row can't move the axis' rule needs ≥ 3 rows; with 1-2 rows the higher-ranked row's `true_count` is shown (accepted, ADR-021). Consequences: worst cases unchanged (`SCORING.md` §2); no migration (bounds unchanged; the Swipe Sort idle example is 37 misses); docs `games/how-many.md` §3/§9, `games/pairs.md` §4/§9, `games/swipe-sort.md` §3/§9, `SCREENS.md` H3. Also add one line to ADR-134 (2) and ADR-136 (1): 'Implemented from ADR-137 (1); before that the shell seeded per player.' Update the file's 'Last updated' date.
